label: QPS (single thread)
comparator: Apache Lucene 10.6.0 (JVM, documents contract: payload in doc values instead of stored fields)
hypothesis: measured (M4, same process, identical results, 2026-11-05): ranking from the mapped checkpoint is 1.5x to 1.9x slower than from the live store on all four corpora. On FiQA the flat varint postings cost most of it: 56% of postings carry a frequency above 1 and missed the one-byte fast path; the two-byte window decoder recovers 1.09x, and the rest needs a block-packed checkpoint posting encoding (a checkpoint format change). On the small corpora, rebuilding a StoredDocument per hit was about 45% of a query; checkpoint hits now decode straight into their results (paired M4, identical results: NFCorpus 1.17x, SciFact 1.11x, memory and FiQA unchanged); the record's JSON metadata parse, 13% of that profile, was still paid per hit. Cut on 2026-11-06 (paired M4, same process, identical results, against main after the block-packed checkpoint): a hit now decodes its record without building the chunk vector and a per-query cache shares repeated metadata values; NFCorpus 1.18x, memory 1.08x, FiQA 1.00x QPS, since hit decode is about 10% of a FiQA query and the exhaustive rank() pass is 82%. Block-max MaxScore was slower than the exhaustive pass at k=100, and a larger hot-list budget doubles serving RSS
